question.text: What is the purpose of a 'Business Risk Assessment' (BRA) that all IFSCA-regulated entities must conduct?

answer.text: To identify, assess, and understand the money laundering and terrorist financing risks faced by the entity based on its products, services, customers, and geographic exposure
To evaluate the profitability and commercial viability of the entity's business model
To determine the credit risk exposure of the entity's loan portfolio
To assess workplace safety hazards and ensure compliance with labour laws

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM IFSCA-01 workbook (p35, p75), a Business Risk Assessment requires every regulated entity to identify, assess and understand its ML/TF exposure across customer, geography, product, service, delivery-channel and transaction factors. This BRA then drives the risk-based approach to AML/CFT compliance. The Trap: Option B sounds like a legitimate business assessment but addresses commercial viability and profitability of the business model — not ML/TF risk. The BRA is specifically scoped to money laundering and terrorist financing. Note: Credit-portfolio risk (Option C) and workplace-safety/labour-law assessment (Option D) are different compliance exercises altogether and fall outside the IFSCA BRA's ML/TF remit.
